slides.texte_overlay:
How to read people
better than most
Watch for changes, not single signs. Crossed arms mean nothing alone. Someone who suddenly goes quiet or changes tone is telling you much more.
Listen to what people talk about most. The topics someone keeps coming back to show what they care about or worry about right now.
Notice how people treat others. The way someone speaks to a waiter or a junior colleague tells you more than how they treat you.
Ask open questions and wait. "How did that feel?" Then stay quiet. People reveal the most in the seconds after a silence.
Learn how people have always behaved. I do five minutes a day of history, art or science, and it taught me that human nature rarely changes.
slides.texte_sophia: I do five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. It taught me that human nature rarely changes.

slides.texte_overlay: Pay attention to energy after time together. Some people leave you lighter, others drained. Your body often knows before your mind does.
Use it to understand, never to manipulate. Reading people well should make you kinder and more patient, not more calculating.
